name: VTE in pregnancy and puerperium
rawContent:
# VTE in pregnancy and puerperium: Core Condition Reference

## Overview
VTE in pregnancy/puerperium includes DVT and PE occurring during gestation or postpartum, with major maternal morbidity/mortality implications.

overview.definition: VTE in pregnancy/puerperium includes DVT and PE occurring during gestation or postpartum, with major maternal morbidity/mortality implications.
overview.epidemiology: Risk increases across pregnancy and peaks in the postpartum period.
overview.pathophysiology: Pregnancy-related hypercoagulability, venous stasis and endothelial changes increase thrombosis risk.

redFlags: Postpartum heavy bleeding with anticoagulation decisions needed

firstLine: CXR and PE imaging pathway (V/Q or CTPA per protocol)
specialistTests: Thrombophilia testing deferred to specialist outpatient context when indicated

diagnosis.criteria: Imaging-confirmed DVT/PE in pregnant or puerperal patient with compatible symptoms.

firstLine: Start therapeutic LMWH when clinical suspicion high unless contraindicated
secondLine: Thrombolysis or advanced PE interventions for life-threatening PE with specialist input

monitoring: Continue anticoagulation for recommended duration; delivery and postpartum anticoagulation planning

drugs.name: Low molecular weight heparin
drugs.dosing: Weight-adjusted therapeutic dosing per local obstetric protocol.

content.prognosis: Good with prompt diagnosis/treatment, but delayed treatment increases maternal and fetal risk.
content.foundationDoctorRole: Recognize symptoms quickly, initiate urgent pathway and anticoagulation under senior guidance, and coordinate multidisciplinary care.
content.escalation: Immediate escalation for suspected PE with instability, hypoxia, or diagnostic delay in high-risk patients.
content.keySafetyConsiderations: Balance thrombosis vs bleeding risk around delivery; involve obstetrics early for procedural timing and neuraxial planning.
